config.title: Build scheduler for priority based jobs

intro.title: Build scheduler for priority based jobs
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a job scheduler that processes tasks based on their priority levels. You will learn to implement a priority queue using arrays and sorting to manage jobs efficiently. The core programming concepts include array manipulation, conditional logic, and function definitions. You will use fundamental JavaScript constructs like arrays, objects, and loops to create a working scheduler that handles high-priority jobs first.
intro.usecase: Priority-based job schedulers are a core pattern in real-world applications where tasks must be executed in an order of importance, not just first-in-first-out. For example, in a customer support dashboard, incoming tickets are automatically prioritized so that critical issues from premium clients are handled before routine inquiries. As a developer, you might implement this in a video rendering queue, where a user's urgent export jumps ahead of other jobs, or in a notification system that sends real-time alerts before batch updates. Mastering this concept allows you to build efficient, user-centric features that manage limited resources intelligently.

objectives: Implement a priority queue data structure to manage job ordering.
Construct a job object with properties for task description and priority level.
Initialize a scheduler function that can accept new jobs and store them.
Manipulate the queue to ensure the highest priority job is always processed first.
Integrate job execution logic that removes and runs the next job from the queue.
Configure the scheduler to handle edge cases like an empty queue.
Apply the scheduler in a simulated environment to process a sequence of jobs.

steps.title: Define the Job class
steps.instruction: Create a Job class with id, name, priority, and duration properties. Use a constructor to initialize these properties.
steps.hint: Define a class with a constructor that takes parameters and assigns them to instance properties.

steps.title: Initialize the scheduler state
steps.instruction: Create a function named Scheduler that initializes three variables: a priority queue, a variable for the current job, and an array for job history.
steps.hint: Declare the Scheduler function and inside it, create variables to store the priority queue instance, current job (initially null), and job history (empty array).
steps.expectedOutcome: A Scheduler function is created with three variables: a priority queue instance, current job (null), and job history array.
successCriteria: The Scheduler function exists and contains variables for priorityQueue, currentJob, and jobHistory.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you've created all three required variables inside the Scheduler function.
steps.feedbackWrong: The Scheduler function or its variables are missing. Create a function named Scheduler with the three state variables inside.

steps.title: Create addJob function
steps.instruction: Inside the Scheduler function, create a function named addJob that takes parameters for name, priority, and duration, creates a new Job instance, and adds it to the priority queue.
steps.hint: Define a function that accepts the job details, instantiates a Job with those values, and pushes it into the queue.
steps.expectedOutcome: The Scheduler function now contains an addJob function that creates Job objects and adds them to the queue.
successCriteria: The addJob function is defined inside Scheduler, takes name, priority, and duration parameters, creates a new Job, and adds it to the queue.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've started the addJob function, but make sure it accepts all three parameters and properly creates a Job instance before adding it to the queue.
steps.feedbackWrong: The addJob function isn't properly defined. It should be inside Scheduler, take three parameters, create a Job, and add it to the queue.

steps.title: Create processNextJob function
steps.instruction: Inside the Scheduler function, define a function named processNextJob that removes the highest priority job from the queue and sets it as the current job.
steps.hint: You can use the dequeue method on the priorityQueue to get the highest priority job, then assign it to a currentJob variable.
steps.expectedOutcome: The processNextJob function is defined and ready to be called to process jobs.
successCriteria: The processNextJob function is defined inside Scheduler, uses dequeue on the priorityQueue, and assigns the result to a currentJob variable.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure the function removes a job from the queue and assigns it to currentJob.
steps.feedbackWrong: The processNextJob function isn't defined correctly. Check the hint and try again.

steps.title: Create completeCurrentJob function
steps.instruction: Inside your Scheduler function, create a function named completeCurrentJob that moves the current job to the history array and clears the current job.
steps.hint: The function should check if there is a current job, push it to the history array, then set the current job to null.
steps.expectedOutcome: A completeCurrentJob function is defined inside the Scheduler function that handles job completion and history tracking.
successCriteria: The completeCurrentJob function exists, checks for a current job, pushes it to history, and clears the current job.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've created the function, but make sure it properly checks for a current job, pushes it to history, and clears the current job.
steps.feedbackWrong: The completeCurrentJob function isn't properly defined. It should check for a current job, move it to history, and clear the current job.

steps.title: Create the main scheduler structure
steps.instruction: Create a main function named 'runScheduler' that will contain the scheduler logic and return an object with the scheduler's public methods.
steps.hint: Define a function that returns an object containing the addJob, processNextJob, and completeCurrentJob functions.
steps.expectedOutcome: You should have a 'runScheduler' function that returns an object with the scheduler's public methods.
successCriteria: The 'runScheduler' function is defined and returns an object containing the scheduler methods.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure your 'runScheduler' function returns an object with the scheduler methods.
steps.feedbackWrong: Create a function named 'runScheduler' that returns an object with the scheduler's public methods.

steps.title: Add job input form
steps.instruction: Inside the Scheduler component's return statement, add a form element with three input fields: one for job name (text), one for priority (number), and one for duration (number).
steps.hint: Create a <form> element with three <input> elements inside. Set appropriate type attributes: 'text' for name, 'number' for priority and duration.
steps.expectedOutcome: A form with three input fields appears in the scheduler UI, ready to accept job details.
successCriteria: The Scheduler component returns a form element containing three input fields with appropriate types.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You added a form, but make sure it has all three input fields (name, priority, duration) with correct types.
steps.feedbackWrong: The form or required input fields are missing. Check that you added a form element with three inputs inside the return statement.

steps.title: Wire addJob to the form submit
steps.instruction: Add an onSubmit event handler to the form element that calls the addJob function with the input values.
steps.hint: Use the onSubmit attribute on the form tag and pass a function that prevents the default form submission behavior, then calls addJob with the job name and priority values.
steps.expectedOutcome: The form will have an onSubmit handler that calls addJob with the input values when submitted.
successCriteria: Handler calls addJob function with input values
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure your onSubmit handler prevents the default form behavior and calls addJob with the input values.
steps.feedbackWrong: The form still needs an onSubmit handler that calls addJob. Check the analogous example for guidance.

steps.title: Add process and complete buttons
steps.instruction: Add two buttons inside the main scheduler structure: one labeled 'Process Next Job' that calls processNextJob when clicked, and another labeled 'Complete Current Job' that calls completeCurrentJob when clicked.
steps.hint: Place the buttons after the form but before the current job and queue display. Use the onClick attribute to wire each button to its corresponding function.
steps.expectedOutcome: Two new buttons appear in the scheduler UI, allowing manual control over job processing and completion.
successCriteria: The scheduler UI includes a 'Process Next Job' button wired to processNextJob and a 'Complete Current Job' button wired to completeCurrentJob.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You added some buttons, but make sure both are present and correctly wired to their respective functions.
steps.feedbackWrong: The required buttons are missing or not properly connected to the scheduler functions.

successCriteria: A job history section is added with a heading and maps over completedJobs to display each job's details.
